summary: Unlock cross-profile repositories, manage GitHub Issues, and open pull requests directly in Git Manager.

features.title: Cross-profile repository access
features.short: Unlock every repository from one profile
features.description: Git Manager always shows that repositories owned by other system profiles exist, but keeps their status, history, files, remotes and actions locked. With Premium, a sudo-capable user confirms their own password once and unlocks every repository for the current mvmOS session, while each Git command still runs as the repository's real owner. Without Premium, nothing is lost: sign in to the corresponding owner profile and manage the same repository there.

features.title: GitHub Issues
features.short: Manage issues with Markdown, checklists and their own branch
features.description: View open and closed GitHub Issues, inspect their details and comments, create new issues, edit an issue's title and body afterwards, and close or reopen them. Creating or editing an issue lets you set its assignees, labels and milestone straight from the repository's own GitHub data. Issue bodies and comments render as Markdown, including clickable task-list checkboxes that save back to GitHub the moment you check or uncheck one — no need to open the editor. A formatting toolbar (headings, bold, italic, quote, code, links, lists, checklists) is available whenever you're writing or editing an issue. Each issue has its own user/issue<number> branch, which you create yourself with one click from the current branch or from the repository's default branch, locally or fresh from the remote. It is never created without asking. Authentication works with either an existing GitHub CLI login or a per-user fine-grained GitHub API token with Issues access.

features.title: Issue settings
features.short: Choose how issues are listed and when their branch opens
features.description: In Git Manager's settings you decide what opening an issue does to your branch: stay on the current branch, which is the default, switch to the issue's own branch only when you are on another issue's branch, or always switch to it, downloading it if it only exists on the remote. You can also split the issue list into issues created by you, issues assigned to you and all the others, in any combination, or combine your created and assigned issues into one section. With nothing selected, all issues are listed together.

features.title: Pull Requests
features.short: Open a pull request from an issue's branch
features.description: Once you're on an issue's own branch, open a pull request straight from Git Manager: choose the source branch and search for the target branch from a list that always puts the repository's default branch first, edit the title and description — prefilled from the issue — and see any pull requests that already target the same branch before opening another. The branch is pushed automatically first if it hasn't been pushed yet, and the finished pull request opens on GitHub to review and merge.
